subject: SLA economic scenarios & pricing grid request
messages:
From: Elaine Cho <elaine@brightcart.com>
To: irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Mark O'Neil <moneil@brightcart.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA options + rough pricing scenarios

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the low tail latencies on the streaming gen. Procurement asked me to consolidate a couple of asks so we can move toward an internal budget decision:

1) Can you send a compact pricing grid with 3–4 SLA bundles (uptime tiers + response windows + escalation coverage) and example monthly $/GPU or $/token economics? We need something the finance folks can line-item.

2) For each bundle, we need the incident credit matrix (what a 4-hour outage vs 24-hour outage looks like) and any caps/exclusions.

3) Is there a simple blended pricing option if we commit to a 12 month Dedicated pool but want a 99.95% target instead of 99.99%? Procurement wants to understand the trade-off quickly.

If you can attach a one-pager or spreadsheet we can circulate, that would be ideal. Preferably by COB Mon so I can include it in our internal review.

Best,
Elaine

From: irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
To: Elaine Cho <elaine@brightcart.com>
Cc: Mark O'Neil <moneil@brightcart.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA options + rough pricing scenarios

Elaine —

Thanks, and great to hear the demo resonated. Attached is a compact pricing grid (SLA_pricing_grid_v1.xlsx) and a one-page Mutual Action Plan (mutual_action_plan_brightcart.pdf). Quick summary of what we included so procurement can scan:

- Bronze (99.9%): standard response windows (8 business-hours for P1), regional failover as optional add-on. Ideal for dev/test and non-critical workloads.
- Silver (99.95%): 4-hour P1 response, 4-hour engineered workaround, 99.95% uptime target, limited escalation coverage to regional oncall.
- Gold (99.99%): 1-hour P1 response, 24/7 escalation to engineering leads, automatic cross-region failover and higher credit caps.
- Blended commit: a negotiable blended price if you commit to a 12-month Dedicated pool — baseline assumes a 20% discount vs hosted list, with trade-offs selectable (e.g., move from Gold SLA to Silver SLA for a further 8–12% reduction).

Incident credits are shown as % of monthly invoice in the spreadsheet with explicit caps and a per-incident maximum. Exclusions and force majeure clauses are summarized on the last tab.

If you want, we can run 3 economic scenarios (current prod, bursty seasonal, and sustained-high-throughput) to show the unit cost impact of choosing Silver vs Gold vs blended commit — I can have those back by EOD Tue.

Next steps: if procurement wants numbers for the 12-month Dedicated commit scenario, I need an estimated monthly committed token/GPU baseline and target uptime (99.95% or 99.99%) so I can produce the blended pricing sheet.

Attaching: SLA_pricing_grid_v1.xlsx; mutual_action_plan_brightcart.pdf

—

From: irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SLA options + rough pricing scenarios — internal ask

Folks — forwarding BrightCart's note. Procurement specifically called out: a compact grid, incident credit matrix, and a quick blended-commit example for 12 months assuming they pick Silver (99.95%).

My suggested play: offer a 12-month Dedicated commit with the following options they can toggle in the spreadsheet:
- Option A: 12mo commit + Silver SLA -> 18% discount off Hosted list (we absorb some margin but keep predictable capacity).
- Option B: 12mo commit + Gold SLA -> 12% discount (higher SLA, smaller %. We keep oncall uplift as add-on).
- Option C: 12mo commit + Silver SLA + limited burst (50% burst capacity) -> 15% discount.

We should also surface a middle-ground — Silver SLA with 24/7 escalation as a paid add-on; call it Silver+. If procurement is price-sensitive they usually take Silver + 24/7 escalation add-on vs Gold full.

Can you both review the attachment (SLA_pricing_grid_v1.xlsx) and comment on whether these ranges are defensible from ops/cost perspectives? I want to get a polished grid out to Elaine by EOD Tue.

Irene
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
To: irene_choi@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA options + rough pricing scenarios — internal ask

Irene —

Reviewed the spreadsheet quickly. A few operational notes:
- 18% for Silver seems aggressive if we have to reserve large Dedicated pools in US-west. Our marginal GPU cost for Dedicated sizing is closer to 25–28% below Hosted list when committed. Offering 18% is fine if we keep burst gating tight and require a firm commit baseline.
- For the incident credit matrix: add a clause that credits for outages related to customer-managed networking or third-party provider actions are excluded.
- Add a practical cap: per-incident credit capped at 50% of monthly invoice for Gold and 30% for Silver. That reduces open liability.

I can ask ops to model the monthly $/committed-GPU and send a quick CSV tonight so you can drop the blended numbers into the spreadsheet.

V
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Cho <elaine@brightcart.com>
To: irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Mark O'Neil <moneil@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA options + rough pricing scenarios

Irene — thanks for the quick turnaround and the materials. A few clarifying points from procurement after a fast pass:

- BrightCart target: 99.95% for core checkout flows (we can accept regional failover for non-core).
- They asked for a blended quote assuming we commit to a 12-month Dedicated pool at 600 committed concurrent tokens-per-second equivalent (they'll provide normalized numbers, but use 600 for your model).
- Can you show a 3-scenario table (base: Silver at 99.95%; conservative: Gold at 99.99%; compromise: Silver+24/7 escalation) with final monthly $ and estimated per-token unit cost? Procurement wants to see the delta to help Ops sign off.
- Also: if BrightCart signs with Silver SLA + 24/7 escalation add-on, can we get an initial 60-day trial of the escalation add-on at no charge so they can validate runbooks? They pushed this as a go/no-go gating item.

If you can get that back by EOD Wed we will present to Finance on Thu.

Thanks —Elaine
From: irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
To: Elaine Cho <elaine@brightcart.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, Mark O'Neil <moneil@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 17:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA options + rough pricing scenarios

Elaine —

Appreciate the clarity — we ran three economic scenarios and attached the updated deck (doc_sign_proposal_BR-2026-778.pdf) plus a CSV with the per-token math. Summary (high level):

- Base: Silver (99.95%) at 600 tps-equivalent committed -> $112,500/mo -> per-token estimate: $0.00019/token (normalized to your supplied baseline)
- Conservative: Gold (99.99%) -> $136,250/mo -> $0.00023/token (includes cross-region standby and larger oncall uplift)
- Compromise: Silver + 24/7 escalation add-on (first 60 days free trial) -> $120,750/mo -> $0.000205/token.

We can do the 60-day trial of the escalation add-on on the condition that BrightCart provides runbook feedback and a short, mutually agreed adoption checklist (we included the template in the MAP). The trial will be limited to the committed pool capacity and excludes 3rd-party networking issues.

I also included the revised incident credit caps we discussed (50%/incident for Gold; 30%/incident for Silver), and the exact force-majeure and exclusion language in the final PDF.

If these numbers look aligned, I'll create a HubSpot quote and send a DocuSign for a 12mo commit with the chosen SLA. Otherwise, flag which line you want to tweak and I can revise quickly.

Best,
Irene
